name: Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)
place: Chajnantor plateau, Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region
description: An interferometer of 66 radio antennas at about 5,000 m altitude that observes millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths. It is run by ESO, North American and East Asian partners together with Chile.
highlights: Its first images were released on 3 October 2011 and it reached full operational status in March 2013.
It studies star and planet formation, dust and molecules in space, and early galaxies.
Its wavelength range is 0.32 to 3.6 mm.
